sentences.text: The only known specimen of Zholsuchus was found in the Turonian-age Upper Cretaceous Bissekty Formation of Dzharakhuduk, Uzbekistan. This animal is known only from scanty material, specifically a right premaxilla, which is one of the bones at the tip of the snout.
The type species of Zholsuchus is Z. procevus.
Zholsuchus was described in 1989 by Lev Nessov and colleagues.
Zholsuchus belongs to the parent group Crocodylia.
Zholsuchus lived between 100.5 and 72.2 million years ago, during the Cenomanian to Campanian stages.
A 2000 review by Glenn Storrs and Mikhail Efimov designated Zholsuchus as a dubious name.
